message: balance(world): populate encounter areas and retire excessive ambient caches safely

replacements.old: Need(State.Chests.TryGetValue(id,out var chest),"Chest not found."); Near(p,chest!.Zone,chest.Position);
replacements.new: Need(State.Chests.TryGetValue(id,out var chest),"Chest not found."); Need(WorldPopulation.ChestEnabled(chest!,Data),"This old cache is no longer available."); Near(p,chest!.Zone,chest.Position);

edits.content:
# Encounter and cache density

Population plans add stable normal-creature IDs around playable encounter areas.
Targets are eight normal instances around starter/dungeon areas and twelve in wilderness, accounting for baseline normal species.
Each region has at most twelve additions. Positions avoid service staff and doors and use valid terrain.
This is a bounded first density pass, not complete ecology across every large region.

Existing IDs, health, death state, and respawn timers remain unchanged.
Restarting does not respawn defeated population entries or add duplicate IDs.
Cities and interiors receive no added hostile creatures.

The starter has one ambient cache. Cities, ordinary settlements, and interiors have none.
Surface wilderness retains one hidden cache. Dungeons and underground regions retain two.
Old excess ambient chest records stay saved but are excluded from discovery, snapshots, and server loot commands.
Special nonambient cache IDs are unaffected. Existing saves are not deleted.

Tests cover deterministic placement, budgets, valid positions, service separation, safe regions, restart state, legacy-ID rejection, and special-cache preservation.
Human density/chest discovery playtesting and economy measurements remain required.
